ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $ \angle AOB=30^\circ$, point P lies on the bisector of $ \angle AOB$, the perpendicular bisector of $ OP$ intersects $ OA$ and $ OB$ at points M and N, respectively. Point E is a point on $ OA$ different from point M, and $ PE=ON=2$. What is the area of $ \triangle POE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect PM, draw PC $\perp$ OA at point C through point P, suppose MN intersects OP at point D,\\
$\because \angle AOB=30^\circ$, OP is the angle bisector of $\angle AOB$,\\
$\therefore \angle MOP=15^\circ$\\
$\because$ MN is the perpendicular bisector of OP\\
$\therefore MN\perp OD$, $MP=MO$\\
$\therefore \angle ODM=\angle ODN=90^\circ$, $\angle MOP=\angle MPO=15^\circ$\\
Also, $\because OD=OD$\\
$\therefore \triangle OMD\cong \triangle OND$\\
$\therefore OM=ON$\\
$\because PE=ON=2$\\
$\therefore PE=OM$\\
$\because MP=MO$\\
$\therefore MP=PE=2$\\
$\because \angle PMA=\angle MOP+\angle MPO=30^\circ$\\
$\therefore \angle PEC=\angle PME=30^\circ$\\
$\because PC\perp ME$\\
$\therefore CE=CM$, $PC=\frac{1}{2}PE=1$\\
In $\triangle CPE$, $CE=\sqrt{3}$\\
$\therefore OE=OM+ME=OM+2CE=2+2\sqrt{3}$\\
$\therefore {S}_{\triangle POE}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot OE\cdot PC = \boxed{1+\sqrt{3}}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, point O is at the lower left, ray OB points to the right, ray OA points to the upper right, and there is ray OP inside ∠AOB. Point M is on OA, point N is on OB, and an oblique line MN is perpendicular to OP and serves as the perpendicular bisector of OP. Point E is also on OA, and from the figure, E is located to the upper right of M, that is, farther from O than M. Then reason: By the coordinate method, take O as the origin, OA as the positive x-axis, and OB forms -30° with OA, so OP is on the angle bisector, with direction angle -15°. Let P = r(cos15°, -sin15°). Because MN is the perpendicular bisector of OP, any point X on it satisfies XO = XP, namely X·P = r^2/2. Point N is on OB and ON = 2, so N = 2(cos30°, -sin30°). Substitute into the perpendicular bisector equation: N·P = 2r cos15° = r^2/2, therefore r = 4cos15°. Thus P = (4cos^2 15°, -4cos15°sin15°) = (2 + √3, -1). Let E = (x, 0). From PE = 2, get (x - (2 + √3))^2 + 1 = 4, so x = 2 or x = 2 + 2√3. When X = (x,0) is on OA and on the perpendicular bisector, x(2 + √3) = r^2/2 = 4 + 2√3, solving gives x = 2, so x = 2 corresponds to point M. Since E is different from M, and in the figure E is on the outside of M, take OE = x = 2 + 2√3. The distance from P to OA is |y_P| = 1, so the area of triangle POE is 1/2 × OE × 1 = 1/2 × (2 + 2√3) = 1 + √3.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, $\angle AOB = 30^\circ$. Point $P$ lies on the bisector of $\angle AOB$. The perpendicular bisector of $OP$ intersects $OA$ and $OB$ at points $M$ and $N$, respectively. Point $E$ is on $OA$ and different from point $M$, and $PE = ON = 2$. What is the area of $\triangle POE$?
raw_record.answer:
Solution: As shown in the figure, connect $PM$, and draw $PC \perp OA$ at point $C$ through point $P$. Suppose $MN$ intersects $OP$ at point $D$.

Because $\angle AOB = 30^\circ$ and $OP$ is the angle bisector of $\angle AOB$, therefore $\angle MOP = 15^\circ$.

Because $MN$ is the perpendicular bisector of $OP$, therefore $MN \perp OD$ and $MP = MO$.

Therefore $\angle ODM = \angle ODN = 90^\circ$, and $\angle MOP = \angle MPO = 15^\circ$.

Also, because $OD = OD$, therefore $\triangle OMD \cong \triangle OND$, so $OM = ON$.

Because $PE = ON = 2$, therefore $PE = OM$.

Because $MP = MO$, therefore $MP = PE = 2$.

Because $\angle PMA = \angle MOP + \angle MPO = 30^\circ$, therefore $\angle PEC = \angle PME = 30^\circ$.

Because $PC \perp ME$, therefore $CE = CM$ and $PC = \frac{1}{2}PE = 1$.

In $\triangle CPE$, $CE = \sqrt{3}$.

Therefore $OE = OM + ME = OM + 2CE = 2 + 2\sqrt{3}$.

Therefore ${S}_{\triangle POE} = \frac{1}{2} \cdot OE \cdot PC = \boxed{1 + \sqrt{3}}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure, point O is at the lower left, ray OB points to the right, ray OA points to the upper right, and there is ray OP inside ∠AOB. Point M is on OA, point N is on OB, and an oblique line MN is perpendicular to OP and serves as the perpendicular bisector of OP. Point E is also on OA, and from the figure, E is located to the upper right of M, that is, farther from O than M.

Then reason: By the coordinate method, take O as the origin, OA as the positive x-axis, and OB forms -30° with OA, so OP is on the angle bisector, with direction angle -15°. Let P = r(cos15°, -sin15°). Because MN is the perpendicular bisector of OP, any point X on it satisfies XO = XP, namely X·P = r^2/2.

Point N is on OB and ON = 2, so N = 2(cos30°, -sin30°). Substitute into the perpendicular bisector equation: N·P = 2r cos15° = r^2/2, therefore r = 4cos15°.

Thus P = (4cos^2 15°, -4cos15°sin15°) = (2 + √3, -1). Let E = (x, 0). From PE = 2, get (x - (2 + √3))^2 + 1 = 4, so x = 2 or x = 2 + 2√3.

When X = (x,0) is on OA and on the perpendicular bisector, x(2 + √3) = r^2/2 = 4 + 2√3, solving gives x = 2, so x = 2 corresponds to point M. Since E is different from M, and in the figure E is on the outside of M, take OE = x = 2 + 2√3.

The distance from P to OA is |y_P| = 1, so the area of triangle POE is 1/2 × OE × 1 = 1/2 × (2 + 2√3) = 1 + √3.
